strategy.summary: Reproduce gh-24551 / PR 24597 on the buggy revision c998b5fcaf06 of scipy (pure-Python change in scipy/stats/_continuous_distns.py, exponnorm_gen). Apply the developer's test_extremely_small_K (parametrized K in 1e-9, 1e-12, 1e-15) and run it. It should fail on the buggy revision because exponnorm logpdf/cdf/sf cancel for small K and miss the standard normal reference at rtol 1e-7, and pass once the erfcx-based branch (K < 1 and u >= 0) is present. The reference is scipy.stats.norm itself, so no mpmath is needed for the transition.

system_packages: libopenblas-dev or any BLAS/LAPACK supported by scipy meson build
pinned_because: python 3.13.11: documented in issue#24551 reproducer system information
numpy 2.4.2: documented in issue#24551 reproducer system information (explicit, numerically relevant)

scipy 1.17.0: documented in issue#24551 reproducer system information; not pinned as a wheel because the reproduction builds scipy from the buggy source tree at c998b5fcaf06, which is the revision that matters
scipy.special.erfcx: no documented constraint and no era table entry; the fixed branch relies on erfcx being present in any modern scipy build, so no version is pinned

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py::TestExponNorm::test_extremely_small_K[K] (added by the PR diff; parametrized over K = 1e-9, 1e-12, 1e-15)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision c998b5fcaf06 with the test diff applied, test_extremely_small_K fails for at least one K: the first mismatched assert_allclose (logpdf, cdf, or sf against norm at x in [-10.5, -3, -1, 1, 3, 10.5]) raises AssertionError. On the fixed revision (the PR 24597 commit with the erfcx branch), all three K parametrizations pass with assert_allclose default tolerance.
strategy.numerical_probe: exponnorm(1e-11).cdf(np.array([-4, 4])) should be approximately [3.16712e-05, 9.99968e-01] (norm.cdf values), buggy output [-9.99968e-01, -3.16712e-05]; use only as a sanity check, the pass/fail transition is decided by the test.

input_output_examples.input: from scipy.stats import exponnorm; import numpy as np; exponnorm(1e-11).cdf(np.array([-4, 4]))

risks: The buggy revision must be the parent of the PR fix; if the checkout includes the fix, the test passes on both sides and no transition is observed.

The test diff is in the middle of a test class (TestExponNorm, near test_sf_small_K); -k selection depends on that class name, so check the actual class name in the checkout before relying on the node id.
The first failing assertion is expected to be logpdf or cdf but this is not confirmed; the test stops at the first mismatch, so the failure message may differ from the issue's cdf output.

K = 1e-15 is indistinguishable from the normal in float64; the test compares to norm directly, so this is fine, but a tolerance-only fix could pass at 1e-15 and fail at 1e-9 or 1e-12, so check all three parametrizations.

Nothing in the evidence shows a platform, sanitizer, or threading requirement; the defect is pure-Python cancellation, so it should reproduce on any architecture. Only the BLAS/LAPACK/Fortran build dependencies are platform-sensitive.

The K threshold changed during review (1e-6 to 1). The PR test at K <= 1e-9 is inside both thresholds, so the transition should not depend on which revision of the threshold is used, but the fixed-side behaviour for K in (1e-9, 1) differs between revisions.
erfcx is assumed available from scipy.special in any modern build; this is not documented as a constraint in the evidence, so it is an assumption, not a pinned fact.
Whether scipy 1.17.0 wheels would reproduce is not tested here; the plan builds from source at the buggy commit, so the installed scipy version is the source tree, not 1.17.0 from PyPI.

oracle.reference_source: scipy.stats.norm logpdf, cdf, sf (standard normal), evaluated at the same x
oracle.why: The test asserts that exponnorm(K) approaches the standard normal as K approaches 0, so the reference is the normal distribution rather than a fixed printed value.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On c998b5fcaf06, exponnorm(K).cdf and related logpdf/sf values at x such as -10.5 or -3 are wrong because the erfc expression cancels for large erfc argument (u = (-x + 1/K)/sqrt(2) large), producing negative or wrong values; assert_allclose at rtol 1e-7 against norm raises AssertionError on the first mismatched method.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision, the erfcx-based branch (used when K < 1 and u >= 0) and the default branch (u < 0) reproduce the standard normal logpdf, cdf and sf to within rtol 1e-7 for K = 1e-9, 1e-12, 1e-15 at all six x values, so all three parametrizations pass.
